anya: Ran a perf sweep this morning comparing NVLink mesh vs PCIe-only on an 8xA100 cluster. Seeing large all-reduce tail latencies for sequence lengths >1024 and frequent KV-cache misses when we enable aggressive batching. Pasting a short profiler excerpt and notes.

anya: profiler snippet (nvtx timeline):
```
step 120: compute 12.3ms | allreduce 18.7ms | wait 5.9ms  <-- NVLink mesh
step 121: compute 12.1ms | allreduce 32.4ms | wait 8.5ms  <-- PCIe-only
backward: reduce_scatter start delayed until 100% compute finishes, little overlap
KV cache miss rate: 14% for prefix reuse workload (compare 3% in single-GPU dev runs)
```

devon: which model / TP/PP config? batch size and sequence lengths?

anya: model: 30B transformer (custom variant), TP=4, PP=1 currently for the runs. micro-batch 1, global batch 8, max_seq 2048 for the long-case. Run command snippet:
```
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
# NVLink run: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
# PCIe-only run: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PCIe NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 python -m distributed.launch ...
```

liam: two quick thoughts: 1) kernel selection — are we falling back to the non-fused attention kernel at seq>1024? That makes compute shorter but increases fragmentation and synchronizations. 2) KV placement — if the KV cache lands on host (or is shuffled between GPUs) we get PCIe/host hops that ruin overlap.

maria: agree with liam. Also, we should verify that reduce_scatter + allgather path is being used (NCCL's optimized path) and not an emulated allreduce. If our gradient hooks do synchronous allreduces inside Python, overlap won't happen. We use gradient bucketing + async hooks in prod; does this run enable that?

anya: it does not — the quick sweep used the default autograd hooks (synchronous). I re-ran one trace with manual async_bucketed_allreduce and saw better overlap but still a ~1.6x allreduce penalty on PCIe compared to NVLink. nvprof NVTX trace shows long allreduce spikes that line up with cross-host PCIe hops.

anya: pasted a minimal timeline showing lack of overlap:
```
[GPU0] compute 0-12ms | allreduce 12-30ms | idle 30-40ms
[GPU1] compute 0-12ms | allreduce 12-30ms | idle 30-40ms
# expected: reduce_scatter should start at ~6ms to overlap last part of compute
```

devon: can you try enabling NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS (if supported) or NCCL_ALGO=Ring vs Tree to see how collective algorithm affects comm cost? also try NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 to force standard NCCL paths. Might expose if CollNet is degenerating.

liam: on the kernel side: ensure compile-time flags pick the fused QKV + attention kernel for seq>1024. Our current kernel selector uses sequence thresholds and batch distribution heuristics; it might flip to a slower kernel if it predicts poor occupancy for TP=4. Worth adding a hard override for experiment.

maria: for KV cache: pin the KV tensors to GPU-local memory and avoid host staging when possible. If we must stage, batch the writes and prefetch into next-step stream so comm/compute overlaps better. Also consider reducing micro-batch size to increase overlap opportunities (tradeoff latency vs throughput).

anya: plan of experiments I can run tomorrow: 1) NVLink vs PCIe runs with async bucketed allreduce enabled, 2) force fused-attn kernel vs fallback to compare compute footprint, 3) vary TP/PP (TP=2,PP=2) to see effect on inter-node allreduce size, 4) run with NCCL_ALGO=Ring and Tree and collect NCCL traces. I'll attach full traces to the perf job.

perf-bot: perf job scheduled: run-id=perf-20250301-41, results will appear in the perf dashboard in ~4h.

devon: if you get a trace, add the nccl_proxy / ibverbs counters too — if InfiniBand/EFA has high QP retries or timeouts that explains spikes. Also test EFA-enabled run (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0) on the same topology to see whether InfiniBand reduces allreduce tail vs PCIe.

anya: good call. For the NVLink machines it's local NVLINK mesh; for cross-host we have EFA. I'll do NVLink-only (intra-node), PCIe-only, and EFA-enabled cross-node runs. I'll leave the thread updated with raw traces and a one-paragraph summary after the dashboard finishes.

liam: one more idea — measure per-layer tensor sizes being allreduced. Very small tensors cause many small collectives that kill throughput; aggregating into larger buckets can reduce overhead significantly.

maria: +1 on bucketing and async hooks. Also check whether our kernel selection increases number of intermediate buffers (more allreduce traffic).

anya: thanks all — will post results in this thread. Starting with the async-bucketed run now (kicking off perf job).
